rendering_check.note: The plate is a large fold-out photographed flat at about 100 dpi, with three vertical and one horizontal crease. It has no frame or grid. main_system_reason: First Street is the longest straight street of the lower town and the spine of both excavated areas we measured. On Marshall's HR plan its west frontage and drain give the best-controlled direction (the plan's meridian is long and ruled); on Mackay's DK-G plan the two sides of First Street and Central Street (sys8) agree with it within about two degrees, but that plan's north arrow is only 46 px long.
notes: We measured two plans of the lower town: Marshall's fold-out of HR Area Sections A and B (1931, Plate XXXIX) and Mackay's plan of the Late I and II levels of the southern part of DK-G Area (1938, Plate XX). Both arrows are lettered only N. Both are archive.org scans at about 100 dpi, so walls are a few pixels wide and lines were fitted to the drawn wall mass; the HR fold-out has creases and no frame, the DK-G plate has a printed grid that we used as the frame check. The HR plan is not orthogonal: the north-south streets and the lanes of Section B share one direction, while High Lane in Section A, Lane 5 in Section B and the westernmost blocks run several degrees differently, so we report them as separate systems. The DK-G First Street and Central Street agree with the HR First Street to within about two degrees. Loop Lane in DK-G is oblique and is kept apart. The plans show the levels exposed at the end of each excavation, mostly Late period by the excavators' terms; Mackay's plate is labelled Late I and II, Marshall's does not separate phases. We did not measure the citadel (SD area, Great Bath), the VS and L areas or Mackay's site plan; they are candidates for a further pass.
